label: Full Game Transition
title: Transitioning to the full game
lead: Updating your mod to the full game (soon!).
bodyHtml:
How can I migrate my mod to the full game?

CUCoreLib is planned to have support initally for mods for both the demo and the full game during the transition period, though this is subject to change later down the line.

This is only possible due to the lower amount of mechanics changes between the demo and the full game.

As such, this page is meant to address the challenges of migrating mods between these builds.

There are two failure classes to plan for:

  • Method signature changes. A method gains, loses, or reorders parameters. A [HarmonyPatch] pinned to the old signature can no longer find its target and throws ArgumentException: Undefined target method during patching.
  • Member-shape changes. A field becomes a property (or a member is renamed). This will throw MissingFieldException: Field not found.

Compatibility fixes handled by CUCoreLib, to watch out for

Demo-era CUCoreLib registration and placement calls remain supported. Your mods do not need changes for these fixes, though this may break hardcoded references.

  • Terrain IDs. The full game reserves indices 36–42 for vanilla terrain. Existing numeric registrations in that range are relocated to >43.
  • Tile queries. Numeric queries such as TryGetDefinition(world.GetBlock(position), out ...) prioritize vanilla tiles, as such. To query a relocated registration directly, use its stable ID or find its current index with TryGetIndex.
  • Liquid IDs. CUCoreLib reserves full-game liquid tile byte 7 for red sludge and starts custom allocation at 8 (7 on the Demo).
  • Generation. Custom terrain, liquids, buildings, and scattered items affect all new layers by default, you may want to adjust your logic accordingly.
  • Wearable refresh. CUCoreLib supplies the full game's optional sprite-swap component when refreshing worn items, while retaining the Demo's original call.
  • Trader stock. The untradeable flag is now present in the full game, and is applied to items with the unobtainable flag.

Detecting which build is running

Below is a list of inital functions that can help determine what version is running, and how to handle specific version logic:

MemberMeaning
CUCoreUtils.IsDemo()true on the demo, false on the full game.
GameBuildInfo.Matches(GameBuild)true when the target flag includes the running build.
[AppliesToBuild(GameBuild.Full)]Restricts a patch family to the full game. Families without it apply to both builds.
 
using CUCoreLib.Helpers;

if (GameBuildInfo.IsFullGame)
{
    // Full-game-only behavior.
}

// Gate an entire Harmony family to one build:
[AppliesToBuild(GameBuild.Full)]
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(SomeFullGameOnlyType), "SomeMethod")]
public static class FullGameOnlyPatch
{
    // Skipped cleanly on the demo
}

Initial changes to help with migration.

In your mods, some code references the demo's Assembly-CSharp.dll, which is different in the full game's version. Some of the known breakages include:

- Body.Eat is Eat(float hungerAmount, float weightGain). On the full game it is Eat(float hungerAmount, float weightGain, int foodType).

To resolve this, use reflection to call the correct overload based on the running build:

using System.Reflection;
using CUCoreLib.Helpers;

// Works on demo, Playtest, and full:
if (GameBuildInfo.IsFullGame)
{
    typeof(Body).GetMethod("Eat", new[] { typeof(float), typeof(float), typeof(int) })
        ?.Invoke(body, new object[] { amount, weight, 0 });
}
else
{
    typeof(Body).GetMethod("Eat", new[] { typeof(float), typeof(float) })
        ?.Invoke(body, new object[] { amount, weight });
}

- BuildingEntity.health is a public field. On the full game it is a public property backed by _health, and its setter also runs CheckDamage().

To resolve this, use CUCoreLib's accessor instead of touching the member directly:

using CUCoreLib.Helpers;

// Before (breaks on the full game):
// building.health -= damage;
// if (building.health < 0.5f) return;

// After (works on demo, Playtest, and full):
building.SetHealth(building.GetHealth() - damage);
if (building.GetHealth() < 0.5f) return;

- GlobalDark.betaBuild is a public field on the demo. On the full game, the field is removed entirely, and the beta-build text is set directly in Awake().

To resolve this, find the text by content instead of by field reference:

using TMPro;
using UnityEngine;

// Before (breaks on the full game):
// TMP_Text betaBuildText = globalDark.betaBuild;

// After (works on demo, Playtest, and full):
TMP_Text betaBuildText = globalDark.GetComponentsInChildren<TextMeshProUGUI>(true)
    .FirstOrDefault(text => text != null &&
        (text.text?.StartsWith("This is a beta build (", StringComparison.Ordinal) == true ||
         text.text?.StartsWith("This is a modded beta build (", StringComparison.Ordinal) == true));

- Locale.GetPauseQuote() takes no parameters on the demo. On the full game it takes a string context parameter.

To resolve this, use reflection to call the correct overload:

using System.Reflection;
using CUCoreLib.Helpers;

// Works on demo, Playtest, and full:
string quote;
if (GameBuildInfo.IsFullGame)
{
    quote = (string)typeof(Locale).GetMethod("GetPauseQuote", new[] { typeof(string) })
        ?.Invoke(null, new object[] { "" });
}
else
{
    quote = (string)typeof(Locale).GetMethod("GetPauseQuote", Type.EmptyTypes)
        ?.Invoke(null, null);
}

- PlayerCamera.CharacterIndexToLocaleName(int index) exists on the demo. On the full game, the method is removed entirely.

To resolve this, check the build and provide a fallback:

using CUCoreLib.Helpers;

// Works on demo, Playtest, and full:
string name;
if (GameBuildInfo.IsFullGame)
{
    // Method removed
    name = "Unknown";
}
else
{
    name = PlayerCamera.CharacterIndexToLocaleName(index);
}

- Name-only Harmony patches become ambiguous when methods gain overloads. For instance, Body.Eat(float, float) with Eat(float, float, int foodType), and WorldGeneration.SetBlock with (Vector2Int, ushort), (int, int, ushort), and (Vector2, ushort).

A [HarmonyPatch(typeof(T), "Name")] attribute that worked on the demo now throws AmbiguousMatchException during PatchAll, aborting the entire mod load.

To resolve this, pin the patch to the specific overload by parameter types. Two approaches work:

using HarmonyLib;
using System.Reflection;

// 1. Pin by parameter types in the attribute
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(Body), "Eat", new[] { typeof(float), typeof(float), typeof(int) })]
public static class EatPatch
{
    [HarmonyPostfix]
    static void AfterEat(Body __instance) { /* ... */ }
}

// Or 2. Use TargetMethod() convention for build-agnostic resolution
[HarmonyPatch]
public static class EatPatch
{
    static MethodBase TargetMethod()
    {
        // Resolve widest overload on full, only overload on demo
        return AccessTools.GetDeclaredMethods(typeof(Body))
            .Where(m => m.Name == "Eat" && !m.IsStatic)
            .OrderByDescending(m => m.GetParameters().Length)
            .FirstOrDefault();
    }

    [HarmonyPostfix]
    static void AfterEat(Body __instance) { /* ... */ }
}

Approach 2 is useful when a single DLL must run on both builds and the overload set differs.

Build system gotchas

When retargeting your mod to build against the full game's assemblies, you'll hit a few build-system issues:

vars.targets auto-detects the Demo. This will be updated for the CCLTemplate, however most mod projects ship a vars.targets that auto-detects the Demo install and prefers the installed CUCoreLib over the sibling build output. To retarget to the full game, pass explicit properties or adjust your build settings:

msbuild YourMod.csproj -restore -t:Build ^
  -p:BaseGamePath="C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Casualties Unknown" ^
  -p:GameAssembliesDir="C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Casualties Unknown\CasualtiesUnknown_Data\Managed" ^
  -p:GameManagedDir="C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Casualties Unknown\CasualtiesUnknown_Data\Managed" ^
  -p:AssemblyCSharpPath="C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Casualties Unknown\CasualtiesUnknown_Data\Managed\Assembly-CSharp.dll" ^
  -p:CUCoreLibDllPath="C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Casualties Unknown\BepInEx\plugins\CUCoreLib.dll"
